tool.name: ATRIUM keyword extraction
tool.description: finds the keywords of documents and their pages with KeyBERT, YAKE or lemma frequency
tool.command:
#import re ## Each document is linked under its collection name, with the suffix that tells the tool its kind; ## the document id (the first column of the table) is that name. #set $suffixes = {'tabular': '.conllu', 'tei': '.teitok.xml', 'xml': '.xml', 'json': '.document.json', 'csv': '.csv', 'txt': '.txt'} #set $known = r'(\.teitok)?\.xml$|\.document\.json$|\.(conllu|json|csv|txt|tsv|tabular)$' export TMPDIR="\${_GALAXY_JOB_TMP_DIR:-\$PWD/tmp}" && #if $method.kind == 'keybert': #if $method.model_source.source == 'staged': export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 && #else: export HF_HOME="\${_GALAXY_JOB_TMP_DIR:-\$PWD/tmp}/hf" && #end if #end if mkdir -p input baselines out/docs out/pages out/records out/paradata "\$TMPDIR" && #set $used = set() #for $i, $doc in enumerate($documents): #set $name = re.sub(r'[^\w.\-]', '_', re.sub($known, '', str($doc.element_identifier), flags=re.IGNORECASE)) or 'document' #if $name in $used: #set $name = $name + '_' + str($i + 1) #end if #silent $used.add($name) ln -s '$doc' 'input/${name}${suffixes.get(str($doc.ext), ".txt")}' && #end for #for $record in $baselines: #set $name = re.sub(r'[^\w.\-]', '_', re.sub($known, '', str($record.element_identifier), flags=re.IGNORECASE)) or 'document' ln -s '$record' 'baselines/${name}.document.json' && #end for
## Failed documents are reported on stderr and skipped, and the run still exits 0: the job fails ## only when no document at all could be read. python3 /app/keywords.py -i input -o out/keywords.csv -d out/docs -p out/pages $per_page --document-json-dir baselines --document-json-out-dir out/records --paradata-dir out/paradata -m '$method.kind' -n $num_keywords -w $max_words -l '$lang' --workers "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" #if $method.kind == 'keybert': #if $method.model_source.source == 'staged': --keybert-model '$method.model_source.model.fields.path' #else: --keybert-model '@KEYBERT_MODEL@' #end if $method.no_mmr --diversity $method.diversity #end if > keywords.log; status=\$?; cat keywords.log; [ "\$status" -eq 0 ] || exit "\$status"; grep -q 'Done\. [1-9][0-9]*/' keywords.log || { echo 'No document yielded keywords: see the messages above.' >&2; exit 1; }; mv out/keywords.csv '$keywords' && mv out/paradata/*_keyword-extract.json '$paradata'

param.name: documents
param.label: Documents
param.help: One job for all of them. CoNLL-U (tabular), TEITOK (tei or xml), ATRIUM document records (json), line tables (csv with a text column) or plain text (txt); a collection's element names become the document ids.

param.name: kind
param.label: Method
param.option: YAKE: statistical, from the text alone, no model
KeyBERT: closest to the document's meaning, with a multilingual sentence-embedding model
Lemma frequency: the most frequent content lemmas (CoNLL-U, TEITOK or records with lemmas)

param.name: source
param.label: Sentence-embedding model (paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2)
param.option: Download it from the Hugging Face Hub in the job (about 0.5 GB)
Use the copy staged on this server

param.name: model
param.label: Staged model
param.help: Staged by an administrator with the data manager 'ATRIUM Hugging Face models'.

validator.message: No copy of paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 is staged on this server.

param.name: no_mmr
param.label: Do not diversify
param.help: By default, Maximal Marginal Relevance keeps near-duplicate keywords apart.

param.name: diversity
param.label: Diversity
param.help: 0: the closest keywords; 1: the most varied.

param.name: lang
param.label: Language
param.help: YAKE's stop words. KeyBERT's model is multilingual; lemma frequency uses the lemmas.

param.name: per_page
param.label: Also per page
param.help: For inputs that have pages: TEITOK, records, line tables, text with form feeds. CoNLL-U has none.

param.name: baselines
param.label: Document records to add to
param.help: ATRIUM document records from an earlier stage, matched to the documents by name; the keywords are added to them. Not needed when the documents are records themselves.

has_text.text: A CSV input needs a 'text' column.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Finds the keywords of each document, and optionally of each page, with one of three statistical methods. It runs the ATRIUM keyword extractor (`ufal/atrium-keyword-extract`_), release @TOOL_VERSION@, on all the documents in one job.
**Methods**
- *YAKE* scores candidate phrases by their position, frequency and spread in the text. No model. - *KeyBERT* picks the phrases whose sentence embeddings are closest to the document's (``paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2``), with Maximal Marginal Relevance against near-duplicates. The model is downloaded in the job, or read from a copy an administrator has staged with the data manager *ATRIUM Hugging Face models*. - *Lemma frequency* ranks the content lemmas; it needs inputs with lemmas (CoNLL-U, TEITOK, or records whose lines carry them), such as the outputs of *ATRIUM NLP enrichment*.
The controlled-vocabulary keywords of the same tool need a language-model service and are not offered here.
**Inputs**
CoNLL-U, TEITOK, ATRIUM document records (for example from *ATRIUM born-digital converter*), line tables with a ``text`` column (lines marked Trash, Garbage, Inverted or Empty are left out), and plain text. A document that cannot be read is reported and skipped; the job fails only if none can.
**Outputs**
- *Keywords* (CSV): one row per document, ``document_id,kw-1,score-1,…``. - *Keywords per document* and, optionally, *per page*: a collection of ``keyword,score`` tables. - *Document records* (JSON): a collection, each record with the ``keywords`` block. - *Paradata* (JSON): the run's provenance, with the components and their licences.
**Licences**
The code is MIT; YAKE is AGPL-3.0; the KeyBERT model is Apache-2.0. The paradata lists each component's licence.
.. _`ufal/atrium-keyword-extract`: https://github.com/ufal/atrium-keyword-extract
